answers.answer: Build three separately shuffled tiers. From top to bottom: 1 card randomly dealt from the 4 Conflict I cards; 5 randomly dealt from the 10 Conflict II cards; then all 4 Conflict III cards in shuffled order. Return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Its final order from top to bottom is: 1 card ... Conflict I; 5 cards ... Conflict II; all 4 Conflict III ... Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.”

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader and the third Agent (Swordmaster) next to the board; 12 troops total, with 3 in their garrison and the other 9 in supply. Each starts with 1 water and one cube at the bottom of each of the four Influence tracks. Starting VP is 0 in a three-player game and 1 in a four-player game.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Each player places 2 Agents ... third Agent ... Swordmaster”; “other 12 are your troops ... place 3 in the circular garrison ... rest in your supply”; “on the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0 space”; “one each, on the bottom spaces of the four Factions”; “Each player takes 1 water.”

answers.answer: Yes. You may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents. After taking it, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn. Plot Intrigue cards may be played during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns, so you may still play one during that Reveal turn, but not later in the phase after it ends.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: “Agent turns are optional: you may take your Reveal turn while you still have Agents left”; “Once you have taken a Reveal turn, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.” Intrigue cards: “during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.”

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up and use one matching Agent icon to send one Agent to an unoccupied board space. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn; one card cannot send multiple Agents. Meet the space’s requirements and pay its costs immediately, before resolving any space or card effects. If you cannot pay, you cannot send the Agent there.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: “play one card ... using it to send one Agent”; “choose only one Agent icon ... one card can't send multiple Agents”; “can't send an Agent to a board space that already has an Agent”; “Costs are paid immediately ... if you can't pay, you can't send your Agent there.”

answers.answer: No. Conspire’s 4-spice entry cost must be paid before effects resolve, so gaining spice from the Agent card cannot cover the cost when you have only 3 spice. After paying the entry cost and placing the Agent, resolve the board-space effect, the card’s Agent box, and the one-space Faction Influence advancement in any order.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: “Costs are paid immediately, before resolving any effects of the space or the played card”; “Gain the effects of the board space, the card's Agent box, and the one-space Influence advancement ... in any order.” Board spaces: “Conspire ... 4 spice.”

answers.answer: Maximum deployment is 5 troops: all 3 recruited this turn plus up to 2 from the garrison. The 2 recruited by the space and 1 by the card can all be deployed; the two additional garrison troops are the cap on troops brought from the garrison. Any recruited troops not deployed go to the garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its four recruits go to the garrison and cannot normally be deployed there.
answers.evidence: Deploying: “any or all troops you recruited this turn ... plus up to two more troops from your garrison”; “Recruited troops you don't deploy go to your garrison.” Rally Troops: “Recruit four troops (not a Combat space, so they go to your garrison).”

answers.answer: Reveal turn steps: (1) reveal all remaining cards in hand, keeping them separate from Agent-turn cards; (2) resolve the Reveal boxes of the cards just revealed, in any order; (3) set Combat strength; (4) clean up. Reveal boxes of cards played on Agent turns are not used. At cleanup, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn steps 1–4: “reveal all cards remaining in your hand”; “gain the effects in the Reveal boxes of the cards you just revealed (not of cards played on Agent turns earlier this round)”; “Clean Up: put all the cards in front of you (from your Agent and Reveal turns) into your discard pile.”

answers.answer: Yes, you may acquire the replacement card from the Imperium Row if you can afford it, because the row refills immediately after each acquisition. Persuasion from multiple sources may be pooled for one card, and Persuasion from one source may be split across multiple cards. Leftover Persuasion cannot be saved and is lost at the end of the Reveal turn. An acquired card goes to your discard pile and is not used immediately. Its Acquire effect happens once at the moment you acquire it.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: row “must always have five cards: refill it immediately”; “may pool Persuasion from multiple sources ... and may split Persuasion from a single source”; “Persuasion can never be saved”; acquired cards “go to your discard pile ... you don't use them right away”; Acquire box effect is “at the moment you acquire the card.”

answers.answer: With 3 troops in the Conflict and 4 revealed swords, strength is 10 (3×2 + 4). If your last troop is removed, strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased by any means, including swords. If strength is over 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Set Strength: “each of your troops in the Conflict is worth 2 strength; each sword ... 1 strength”; “if your last troop is ever removed, your strength becomes 0 and can't be increased by any means”; “if over 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again.”

answers.answer: Starting with the First Player and proceeding clockwise, each player with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass. Passing earlier does not prevent playing later. Combat resolves once all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. “When you win a Conflict” Intrigue cards are played only after winning, before the next phase.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: “starting with the First Player and continuing clockwise, each player with at least one troop ... may play any number ... or pass”; “not required to pass just because you passed earlier”; “Once all players involved in Combat pass consecutively, resolve the Combat”; win-trigger cards “only after you've won, before moving to the next phase.”

answers.answer: A and B tie for first, so neither wins; each receives the second reward. C beats D for the remaining rank and receives the third reward in this four-player game; D receives nothing. A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward, including in two- and three-player games. A tie for third yields nothing. A player with 0 strength receives no reward. After rewards, troops go to their owners’ supplies, not their garrisons.
answers.evidence: Ties: “tied for first place — no one wins ... each tied player receives the second reward”; in a 4-player game “the other two still compete for the third reward.” Resolve Combat: ordinary third place gets the third reward in four-player games. Also: “Tied for second ... each receives the third reward”; “Tied for third — nothing”; “A player with 0 strength receives no reward”; troops go to “supply (not their garrison).”

answers.answer: During Phase 4: Makers, after Combat, add one bonus spice from the bank to each of the Great Flat, Hagga Basin, and Imperial Basin if that space has no Agent. Bonus spice accumulates across rounds while a Maker space remains empty. Normal harvesting occurs when an Agent visits: Imperial Basin yields 1 spice plus accumulated bonus, Hagga Basin 2 plus bonus, and the Great Flat 3 plus bonus. If an Agent moves away before Makers, the space is empty at that check and gains bonus spice.
answers.evidence: Makers: “Check each of the three board spaces with a Maker icon: The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, and Imperial Basin. If a space has no Agent on it, place 1 spice ... as bonus spice.” Board spaces give base harvest plus bonus; clarification: “if an Agent moves away ... and it's still empty in Phase 4, bonus spice does accumulate there.”

answers.answer: The game does not end immediately when someone reaches 10 VP mid-round. At the end of the round in Recall, it ends if anyone is at 10 or more VP or the Conflict Deck is empty; revealing the last Conflict triggers the end at that same end-of-round check. Players first resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then the player with the most VP wins. Tiebreak order: spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops (not troops in supply), then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Scoring: “at the end of a round (Phase 5: Recall)” if 10+ VP or Conflict Deck empty; “first, players may play and resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards”; tiebreakers listed spice → Solari → water → garrisoned troops → most recently took a Reveal turn.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence you gain 1 VP, which you lose if you drop below 2 and regain if you reach 2 again. At 4 Influence you earn that space’s bonus, which you keep even if you later drop below 4; you can earn it again by dropping back and re-advancing. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance token and its VP. An opponent takes it by rising to a higher space than its holder; tying does not take it. If the holder loses Influence while another player was tied with them, that previously tied player takes it (if several were tied, the holder chooses one).
answers.evidence: Faction Influence: “At 2 Influence you gain a VP (lost if you drop below 2, regained if you reach 2 again)”; at 4 “you do not give the bonus back ... can even earn it again”; Alliances: first to 4 takes token; opponent must rise to a “higher” space; holder losing Influence while tied transfers token to previously tied player.

answers.answer: If you lose 1 Influence from 5 while tied at 5 with two opponents, one of those previously tied opponents takes the Alliance; when several were tied, the former holder chooses which one. If instead you are the only player at 4 and fall to 3, you lose the token and it returns to the board because no player has 4 or more to take it.
answers.evidence: Alliances: “If the holder loses Influence while previously tied with another player, the previously tied player takes it; if several were tied, the holder chooses one.” Holder loses the token at 3 or less; “if no player has 4 or more to take it, return it to the board.”

answers.answer: Discarding means a card from your hand (unless otherwise specified); it goes to your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from your hand, discard pile, or in play to the game box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or a card instructs you to trash itself. You cannot reshuffle an empty deck early just to inspect its top card; reshuffling happens when unable to draw, and specific clarifications say an empty deck cannot be inspected by effects such as Paul Atreides’ ability or Poison Snooper.
answers.evidence: Trashing cards: discard is “a card from your hand ... it goes to your discard pile”; trashing removes from hand/discard/in play; Reserve cards return to Reserve; optional unless cost or self-trash instruction. Deck exhaustion: reshuffle only when unable to draw; “You can't reshuffle early — e.g., Paul Atreides' ability or Poison Snooper can't look at the top card of an empty deck.”

answers.answer: The controller gets 1 Solari whenever any player, including the controller, sends an Agent to Arrakeen or Carthag; control of Imperial Basin pays 1 spice. Winning a Conflict that rewards control of one of these spaces places your Control marker there, replacing an opponent’s marker. If a matching Conflict is revealed later for a space you already control, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Control: winning a Conflict titled for Arrakeen, Carthag, or Imperial Basin places/replaces the marker. “While it's there, you receive the bonus whenever any player ... sends an Agent there: 1 Solari ... or 1 spice.” Defensive bonus: when a Conflict card is revealed for a space you control, “you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict.”

answers.answer: In two-player play, House Hagal is a third spoiler Rival. Setup: choose an unused color, put one cube at the bottom of each Influence track, put remaining cubes in its supply, and leave its garrison without troops. Remove the three Arrakeen cards marked “1P,” shuffle the remaining Hagal cards, and place the deck and its three Agents near its supply; use no Rival Leader or solo difficulty rules. After each First Player Agent turn, it takes an Agent turn if it has an Agent left, up to three turns per round; it does not act after the other human’s turn or after a Reveal turn. It never Reveals. It does not collect resources, earn Conflict rewards, or score VP, but it can take and hold Faction Alliances.
answers.evidence: Two-player House Hagal Rival setup and Agent turns sections: specified cube setup, no troops in garrison, remove three “1P” cards, three Agents; acts after each First Player Agent turn if able, maximum three; “It never takes a Reveal turn”; “does not collect resources ... earn Conflict rewards or score VP”; “It can take and hold Faction Alliances.”

answers.answer: If the indicated space is occupied, keep revealing until an eligible unoccupied space appears. If the card shows two spaces, use only the option matching current conditions; if that applicable option is occupied, draw a new card rather than switching options. Immediately reshuffle the Hagal deck if it is empty or a Reshuffle card appears, then continue revealing. Ignore normal space costs, requirements, and effects; resolve only the revealed card’s icons and instructions. Each troop icon recruits from supply: deploy it if this is a Combat space, otherwise put it in the garrison. Whenever Hagal sends an Agent to a Combat space, it must also deploy up to two available garrison troops (one if only one, none if empty). Harvest Spice follows its card instructions; remove harvested bonus spice from the space and return it to the bank.
answers.evidence: Agent turns: “otherwise keep revealing until an eligible unoccupied space appears”; two-space card occupied option means draw new card, never switch; reshuffle immediately on empty deck or Reshuffle card. “Ignore the normal costs, requirements and effects”; troop deployment and Harvest Spice rules are stated in the Rival section.

answers.answer: If Hagal has at least one troop in the Conflict, at the start of Combat reveal a Hagal card; if it is Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again until obtaining a card with its sword bonus. Ignore all except its sword icons and add that strength to 2 per deployed troop. Hagal receives no reward for its rank but occupies that rank when humans receive rewards; it can hold Alliances. If it wins a Conflict for a space a human controls, remove that human’s Control marker and Hagal does not replace it. In a two-player game an ordinary third-place finish is unavailable, but human players tied for second each receive the third reward.
answers.evidence: Combat strength procedure: if it has a troop, reveal a card and repeat if Reshuffle; count sword icons plus 2 per deployed troop. It “receives no reward for its rank, but it still occupies that rank”; Alliance rules allow it to take/hold Alliances; if it wins for a human-controlled space, remove marker and do not replace. Tie rules: tied second receives third reward even in two-player games.
